newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Stocks soar on gasoline build.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Stocks soar on gasoline build.

text.p: Singapore weekly light distillate stocks took the market by surprise and soared, mainly due to a gasoline build, traders said on Thursday.
Gasoline, reformate and naphtha stocks rose 1.497 million barrels to 6.704 million barrels -- highest since stocks were 6.817 million barrels in the week ending July 17, 1996.
"It is quite surprising it's so high," said one oil major.
Traders said although a lot of arbitrage barrels were heading to Asia from the West, the build in Singapore was mainly gasoline barrels.
"Nobody really stores naphtha here...if you have the cargoes, it will be committed,' said another trader at a major oil company. "Plus, naphtha storage is very expensive."
Bearish traders said not all the gasoline barrels were committed, and the market was still on the long side.

The Singapore fob market was dull ahead of the long weekend with a major unable to attract any bids for 50,000 barrels of 97-octane unleaded gasoline at $28.80 per barrel, lifting April 11-26. On Wednesday, two cargoes of the grade traded at $28.80 and $28.75.
April lifting unleaded 95-octane was bid/offered at $28.00/$28.10, traders said.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued its tender for its May 1-15 requirements - 250,000 barrels each of leaded and unleaded 95-octane reformate, a company official said.
The tender closes April 1 and is valid for two days.
CPC just last week bought through tender, 250,000 barrels of unleaded reformate at $28.60 per barrel, cost and-freight Taiwan for April 16-30 arrival.
The naphtha market also lacked any firm direction with April
swaps largely unchanged at $22.85/$23.10 per barrel and May at $22.60/$22.90.
